articleTitle: DESIGN OF FORCE PLATE FOR GAIT ANALYSIS
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Gait analysis provides a simple approach to identifying biomechanical abnormalities in walking and running. Force plates, commonly used in biomechanics laboratories, serve as pedagogical tools to explain motion dynamics and kinematics. They measure ground reaction forces, crucial for understanding the loads associated with human activity. In cases of amputation, force analysis is vital to avoid overloading, which risks boneimplant interface damage, and underloading, which unnecessarily prolongs rehabilitation. Modern sensor technology and advanced data acquisition systems have simplified force analysis. A force plate is a metal platform embedded with sensors that generate electrical signals proportional to the applied force. This project focuses on developing a cost-effective, highly sensitive prototype force plate. The system incorporates signal conditioning using a deflected control card, instrumentation amplifiers, and linearization circuits for individual pressure sensors integrated into a rubber mat. Creating a robust optical force platform for research involves systematic steps. It begins with understanding biomechanics and the types of force transducers used, followed by data acquisition involving sampling, signal amplification, processing, and calibration to ensure accuracy. Using force and weight data from the prototype, gait analysis was performed on volunteers with abnormalities such as diplegic and hemiplegic patterns. This demonstrates the potential of the low-cost force plate to analyse and address gait issues effectively.

articleTitle: Recognition of Lower Limb Movements From the Time Domain Features of Surface EMG and Catboost Classifier
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: People who have lost lower limbs due to accidents, trauma, or diseases often need assistance with daily activities. Patients with transfemoral amputations typically use passive prosthetics, but recent research has focused on surface electromyography (sEMG)-enabled prosthetic knees to improve quality of life. However, identifying effective EMG biomarkers for accurately detecting locomotion modes remains a challenge. This study aims to classify wireless SEMG signals from lower limb muscles into five modes—level walking, stair ascent and descent, and ramp ascent and descent—using time-domain features and the CatBoost classification algorithm. sEMG signals from six muscles (rectus femoris, biceps femoris, tibialis anterior, medial gastrocnemius, vastus lateralis, and semitendinosus) were analyzed. Time-domain features, such as root mean square, integrated EMG, mean absolute value, waveform length, Willison amplitude, skewness, entropy, zero crossing, and variance, were extracted and used to train both CatBoost and support vector machine (SVM) algorithms. Leave-one-out cross-validation assessed classification accuracy and stability. CatBoost achieved an accuracy of 83%, outperforming SVM's 72%, with statistically significant results (p<0.05) across all locomotion modes. The study demonstrates that tree-based models can classify lower limb EMG signals and could aid in developing active prosthetic limbs. The approach is also promising for broader EMG applications, including muscle-computer interfaces and rehabilitation. Future work will explore deep learning algorithms to improve accuracy further.

articleTitle: Design and Development of a Gait Analysis System using Force Sensitive Resistor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Gait analysis is essential for evaluating locomotor function, rehabilitation progress and the diagnosis of gait disorders. Traditional methods of gait event detection often involve expensive and cumbersome equipment. This study outlines the design and development of an affordable, portable, reliable system for detecting the gait events using Force Sensitive resistors (FSRs). Force Sensitive Resistors (FSRs) were positioned on the insole to measure pressure changes at the heel and fore foot, corresponding to key gait events like Heel Strike (HS) and Toe Off (TO). A microcontroller-based data acquisition system was developed to record and process the FSR signals in real time. The signals are subjected to noise filtering to accurately identify the gait events. The developed system is evaluated through a series of walking trials involving healthy subjects. The detected gait events are validated against a reference motion capture system. This FSR based gait event detection system offers a cost effective and user- friendly solution for clinical gait analysis and rehabilitation monitoring. Its portability and ease of use makes it suitable for use at clinical settings.

articleTitle: Substantia Nigra Segmentation in 7T MRI Using a 3D UNet Architecture for Enhanced Parkinson's Disease Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: High Resolution Magnetic Resonance Imaging provides detailed structural information of the soft tissues in the clinical environment. The Substantia Nigra (SN) plays a critical role in motor control and is a key region which can be affected in neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson's disease. The precise segmentation of SN helps us in early diagnosis, treatment planning and disease progression. This study proposed a 3D UN et deep learning architecture for the segmentation of the Substantia Nigra. The suggested model was trained and validated with 7T Structural MRI scans ATAG dataset. The Quantitative analysis metrics like Dice Coefficient, Soft Dice Coefficient, Intersection over Union, Dice Loss, and Precision shows significant improvements in segmentation accuracy compared to the traditional segmentation algorithms, with implications for enhancing clinical workflows in the diagnosis and management of Parkinson syndromes.

articleTitle: Human Activity Recognition via Wi-Fi CSI and VAE-CNN-BiLSTM Hybrid Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Human Activity Recognition (HAR) is vital across multiple applications, such as healthcare monitoring, smart home systems, and surveillance. Recently, Wi-Fi channel state information (CSI) has gained attention as a valuable data source for HAR, owing to its non-intrusive nature and capacity to capture detailed spatial information. This paper introduces a deep learning framework that combines variational autoencoders (VAEs), convolutional neural networks (CNNs), and bidirectional long short-term memory (BiLSTM) networks to achieve high-accuracy HAR using Wi-Fi CSI data. The proposed hybrid VAE-CNN-BiLSTM model utilizes spatial information encoded in CSI matrices to extract discriminative features crucial for recognizing different activities. The VAE component captures a compressed representation of the high-dimensional CSI data, enhancing the model's robustness and generalization. The CNN layers then capture spatial features from raw CSI data, identifying both local and global patterns, which are further processed by the BiLSTM layers to capture the temporal dependencies and dynamic patterns associated with human activities. To evaluate the model, we conducted experiments on a publicly available Wi-Fi CSI dataset for human activity recognition in both line-of-sight (LOS) and non-line-of-sight (NLOS) indoor environments, comparing its performance with other state-of-the-art deep learning models. The results indicate that the hybrid VAE-CNN-BiLSTM model achieves superior accuracy, with classification rates of 88.9% in LOS and 88.2% in NLOS scenarios, demonstrating its effectiveness in accurately distinguishing various human activities.

articleTitle: Automated Detection of Micro-Expressions Using Time and Frequency Domain Features of Facial Electromyography
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Facial Electromyography plays crucial role in the field of psychological evaluations by employing it in emotion detection and Micro-Expression Recognition (MER) due to its ability to detect facial muscle activity. The non-invasive behaviour and inter-subject variations can be leveraged by psychologists for psychotherapy and deception detection during therapy sessions. Micro-expressions (MEs) are low intensity and involuntary facial expressions that said to reveal true emotions which are often suppressed. In this study, an attempt has been made to detect and recognize Micro-Expression using Facial Electromyography. In this study, four emotion classes: - Happy, Sad, Fear and Anger are considered. The target muscle regions include Mentalis Region, Zygomaticus Region, Frontalis Region, and Orbital Region. The participants were presented with emotional videos, while voluntarily suppressing emotions with Facial EMG (fEMG) obtained simultaneously. The data was pre-processed and segmented based on Action Unit (AU) Coding. Temporal-domain features such as Mean Absolute Value (MAV), Root Mean Square (RMS), Variance (V AR), Integrated EMG (iEMG)and Zero Crossing Factor (ZCF) are extracted. Additionally, Spatial- domain features such as Mean Frequency (MF), Median Frequency (MDF) and Total Power (TP) are obtained. The classification of Micro-expressions is performed using Random Forest algorithm. This approach resulted in a mean Fl-score of 0.8525 and these insights play an essential role in decoding suppressed emotions.

articleTitle: EEG-Based Eye Blink Detection and Interpretation for Human-Computer Interaction and Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: This research develops a real-time Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) for interpreting eye blinks as a means of hands-free communication, particularly useful for individuals with limited mobility or in high-focus tasks. Combining machine learning (ML) and signal processing, the study detects voluntary eye blinks with high accuracy. Data from 20 participants were analyzed using a random forest classifier, achieving accuracy between 85.29% and 92.15%. A peak detection method further improved blink detection accuracy to over 98%. This system enhances accessibility in various interactive environments, improving life quality for those with disabilities.

articleTitle: AI based Assistive Communication System for Multiple Sclerosis and Paralysed Patient
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The paper describes communication way between Multiple sclerosis's (MS) patient with Brain Computer Interface (BCI). In MS patient immunity system attacks the protective sheath that causes communication problems between Brain and Body. Multiple sclerosis's (MS) patient may have different disabilities such as talk, walk, hear and lack of coordination among the body parts. MS patient can be communicating with the computer using Brain Computer Interface. Brain Computer interface (BCI) read the data from brain controlled electrodes which is placed over the skull. By implementing the Artificial Intelligence (AI) based algorithms, which can predict the patient thoughts and feelings and display patient condition. Also reactivate the disorder parts of the body.

articleTitle: EEG Data Classification of Odia Words Using ML and DL for BCI Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) enables direct communication between the brain and external devices by interpreting brain signals for neurodegenerative disorder patients. BCI-based solutions for regional language-speaking patients with neurodegenerative disorders need datasets in patients' native languages. However, India-specific BCI research lacks appropriate Indian language-specific BCI datasets. For example, Odia, one of the prominent Indian languages spoken by 35–40 million individuals in India, does not have sufficient language-specific BCI datasets. To address this gap, we developed an Electroencephalograph (EEG) based Odia BCI dataset featuring EEG signal samples of commonly spoken Odia words. Using the OpenBCI Cyton device, EEG recordings are collected from a volunteer who speaks Odia language. Our dataset contains EEG data for 100 commonly used Odia words. For each word, 10 BCI samples were recorded. The data is pre-processed using wavelet convolution. We classified the dataset using four, five, and six class classifiers by training the dataset using DL and ML classification algorithms such as SVM, Naive Bayes, and GBM. We achieved the highest accuracy for the Odia vocal BCI dataset for four, five, and six classes, respectively, 85%, 88%, and 71.67%.

articleTitle: A Study on the Effectiveness of Concentration and Co-Ordination Exercise Tool Among Normal Population
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The invention related to the psychology, pedagogy, medicine and physiology. The aim of the experiment is to check and improve the level of concentration and brain-eye-hand coordination among children by daily practicing Concentration and Coordination Exercise Tool. Exercising the brain regularly is one of the easiest and most effective ways to reduce the symptoms of mental retardation and other disabilities. A quantitative method was adopted for the study. The tool used was Concentration and Co-ordination exercise tool developed by Coexin Technologies Healthcare Private Limited. There were different type of strings were used for the study. Karl Pearson's Product Moment Correlation and paired samples t-test was used to analyse the collected data. The research reveals that there is significant difference between pre-test and post-test of time and error in design strings and there is a significant level of improvement in concentration and coordination among children after the exercise of Concentration and Coordination Exercise Tool. Also the research showed that the memory got enhanced, hand writing improved, self-confidence improved, concentration improved and coordination improved. [1], [2] and [3]

articleTitle: Analysis of Muscle Activation in Lower Limb Using Markerless Motion Capture System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The investigation of this study involves, comparing the Electromyogram (EMG) data with the musculoskeletal modeling data to understand the patterns of muscle activation while performing squats. Muscle activation during movement, and the integration of real-time physiological data with advanced biomechanical simulations offers a comprehensive approach in uncovering insights into human motor control. This work highlights the impact of body mass index (BMI) on muscle activity during squats. 12 subjects are selected for EMG acquisition for four Lower limb muscles Bicep Femoris, Rectus Femoris, Tibialis Anterior and Lateral Gastrocnemius. The Markerless motion capturing was performed using OpenCap software for the subjects. Muscle activation is computed for both, with sEMG and OpenSim Musculoskeletal Modelling respectively, and the correspondence between measured and simulated activation is assessed. These further sheds light on the modeling system's ability to accurately deliver the real-world muscle activation responses. The obtained results show normal subjects have higher and stable muscle activation while comparing with lean and obese individuals.

articleTitle: Effectiveness of Cognitive Training on Coordination and Concentration Among Children with ADHD
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of cognitive training intervention on coordination and concentration in children with Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD). The intervention incorporated the Gross Motor Coordination Exercise Tool (GMCET), developed by Coexin Technologies Healthcare Pvt. Ltd.,. Eight children diagnosed with ADHD participated in an eight-week cognitive training program using GMCET. Pre- and postintervention assessments, including the Letter Cancellation Test, Finger Dexterity Apparatus, and the ADHD Rating Scale, revealed significant reductions in hyperactivity and inattention, alongside improvements in finger dexterity and concentration. The results suggest that cognitive training with GMCET may be an effective for enhancing both cognitive and motor functions in children with ADHD.

articleTitle: Detection of High Prospective Value in the Diagnosis of Doubtful Melanocytic Skin Lesions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The most aggressively spreading cancer found among all type of cancers is Skin Cancer. The traditional technique focuses on improving the accuracy of detecting melanocytic skin lesions, which may be benign or malignant like melanoma. At its heart is a convolutional neural network (CNN) that recognizes patterns in dermoscopic images suggestive of malignancy. The intent of the study is to develop an approach that can be used as a tool, which not only increases diagnostic precision but also decreases unnecessary biopsies of benign lesions. The method investigates a number of challenges like unbalanced dataset problem for classification, difficulty in interpreting complex dermoscopic images and generalizing models to data unseen before. To cope with these issues and enhance the model robustness, data augmentation and cross-validation are adopted. The findings show high performance of classification, which could translate to more effective skin cancer diagnostics that ease the burden on health care systems.

articleTitle: Analyzing P300 Signals to Assess Undergraduate Attention Span Using Impulse Neiry BCI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The study on brain signals to understand working memory in undergraduate students has yielded promising results. However, the challenge remains in accurately assessing different brain activities. This work seeks to measure concentration in cognitive performance, offering a detailed dataset that tracks how individuals respond to cognitive tasks. A virtual reality-based solution has proven effective in capturing the P300 signal, providing a more focused and accurate measurement platform. The study aims to evaluate the efficacy of P300 signals as indicators of attention and cognitive engagement in educational settings. A brain-computer interface system, Impulse Neiry, captured and analyzed P300 signals from undergraduate students while performing various cognitive tasks. User attention span was evaluated by measuring parameters such as session duration and interaction frequency with the software, offering insights into the system's usability. The results indicated that participants experienced about 35% deeper relaxation, and their attention spans increased by 18.97% compared to baseline engagement levels.

articleTitle: MODWT Based Analysis of Facial EMG for Assessing Muscle Fatigue: Implications for Rehabilitation and HCI Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The accurate assessment of muscle fatigue is crucial for enhancing rehabilitation protocols and developing sophisticated human-computer interaction (HCI) systems. In this study, an attempt has been made to assess the progression of fatigue in the facial muscles with the help of surface electromyography (sEMG) and the Maximal Overlap Discrete Wavelet Transform (MODWT). The signals are recorded from the left and right frontalis muscles of fifty volunteers during a controlled time contraction protocol. After rigorous signal pre-processing, limited segmentation is executed, isolating the initial and terminal six-second intervals as non-fatigue and fatigue epochs, respectively. To capture the intricate dynamics of muscle fatigue, the MODWT utilizing the Daubechies (db4) wavelet is applied. Wavelet power is extracted across all decomposition levels, revealing a marked reduction in median of wavelet power during fatigue conditions. Additionally, statistical features were computed, providing further insights into muscle fatigue progression. These results underscore the efficacy of wavelet-based sEMG analysis as a robust tool for enhancing the accuracy of muscle fatigue assessment, with significant implications for both rehabilitation strategies and the development of adaptive HCI systems.

articleTitle: Association of Neurological Family Health History in Parkinson's Diseases
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a neurodegenerative disorder primarily affecting elderly people. While the exact cause of idiopathic PD is still unknown, a family history of the condition has been observed in 10 to 15 percent of cases. In addition, Mendelian inheritance patterns are seen in about 5% of cases. In this study we aimed to assess the significant correlation between the development of PD with individual's family's neurological health history. Here we have considered total 13 specific questionnaire related to the subject's neurological family history. The statistical attribution has been made for both uncategorized and categorized by sex. There are notable correlations observed between the PD patient and the history of neurological disorders in family members. Here, we saw that most of them-such as anxiety, depression, Alzheimer's disease, and Parkinson's disease-are protective in nature, while very few-such as the multiple sclerosis (OR-3.25) of the paternal grandmother, the dystonia (OR-1.92) maternal grandmother, and the schizophrenia (OR-1.65) of the mother-act as risk factors. These figures also demonstrate how important family history is in determining the likelihood that the next generation will develop Parkinson's disease.

articleTitle: Adaptive Algorithm Based Text to Braille Conversion for Visually Impaired People
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: This paper introduces a sophisticated communication system tailored for individuals with visual impairments, merging Braille with modern digital technology. The system employs the ESP8266 microcontroller for its WiFi capabilities, serving as the central processor. Text inputs received via WiFi are processed by the ESP8266, activating six solenoid valves positioned to produce Braille patterns. This seamless integration of traditional Braille with WiFi connectivity allows real-time text-to-Braille conversion, enhancing accessibility. Advanced error detection and correction mechanisms ensure accuracy, while adaptive algorithms adjust valve activation for consistent tactile feedback in various environments. The system's flexibility enables integration with additional sensory feedback mechanisms, like audio cues, enriching user interaction. By meticulously combining hardware and software, this Paper sets a new standard in Braille communication systems for visually impaired individuals.

articleTitle: WEBEEG- A Web Based Application for EEG Seizure Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Accurate and timely detection of seizures in epilepsy always remain as a challenge in clinical practice, often requiring visual analysis of large amount of data. In this paper we present a novel web-based application for real time detection of seizures from long term EEG recordings. The application leverages a serialised deep learning model for prediction of seizures, integrating it into a web application developed using streamlit. Features of the web application includes interactive EEG data visualisation, seizure event detection and identification of seizure affected channel. Any user without a prior coding knowledge can easily interact with the application through a web browser, making it widely accessible, ultimately reducing the workload of clinicians in diagnosing epilepsy.

articleTitle: SSVEP Speller Implementations Across Desktop, Web, and Mobile Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: This study explores the implementation of steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) stimuli generation across various platforms to advance brain-computer interface (BCI) accessibility and usability. BCls provide assistive capabilities for people with diseases like spinal cord injury (SCI), Stroke, and Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) by facilitating direct communication paths between the brain and external equipment Creating visual stimuli at specific frequencies to produce reliable neural responses is a basic challenge for BCls based on SSVEP. We ensured outstanding speed and device and browser synchronization by effectively rendering stimuli on web-based systems using WebGL. To create a seamless user experience, we combined WebGL with Web View for mobile devices, improving rendering speed and compatibility. Our work discusses the implementation of Psychopy and WebGL in providing reliable SSVEP stimuli through this multi-platform method. Comparative findings between desktop, online, and mobile implementations show how flexible and scalable our approach.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-based Consciousness Assessment in Disorders of Consciousness Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Refinements in technology have enabled the use of various machine learning methods to improve the evaluation of disorders of consciousness (DOC) patients. This study investigates the application of multiple regression models for consciousness assessment of DOC patients based on EEG features extracted across different frequency bands. Absolute power, relative power, and symbolic transfer entropy are the features considered in the study. The paper implements five regression models: linear regression model, elastic net, support vector regressor, XGBoost, and random forest. Among the models, XGBoost demonstrated the highest predictive accuracy with the highest coefficient of de-termination: 0.855, and the lowest mean square error: 0.111, and the mean absolute error: 0.114. The study highlights XGBoost's effectiveness in assessing consciousness through EEG features, providing a promising tool to improve clinical evaluations and treatment strategies for patients with impaired consciousness.

articleTitle: Towards Building Cognitive Brain Computer Interfaces for Controlling Neural Variability During Repetitive Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation Treatment in Depression
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Depression is a widespread mental health disorder characterized by persistent low mood, anhedonia, and cognitive deficits. Many studies in the past have assessed the use of a repetitive form of Transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) as an intervention in a form that is approved by regulatory bodies such as the FDA. Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) are increasingly being used to study neural dynamics and their potential to enhance cognitive functioning in clinical populations. In this study, we investigate whether cognitive states matter for TMS treatment in Depression. We simultaneously administered rTMS as we acquired electroencephalography (EEG) to study the cognitive state effects in two different groups-Depressed (N=9) and Healthy controls (N=8), during resting state and for various cognitively engaging tasks. We then specifically computed the strength of activations in the fronto-parietal network (FPN) versus the default mode network (DMN) during stimulation for their significance in reflecting the trade-off in the cortico-limbic circuit activations. Our findings suggest that the cognitive state of an individual should be considered to control for effective and selective recruitment of FPN in contrast to DMN cognitive circuits with rTMS intervention. We finally present results upon implementing the paradigm in one longitudinal study participant, who undertook rTMS treatment for 6 weeks in a precisely cognitively calibrated design mentioned above. This study's findings offer a foundation for developing a closed loop brain-computer interfaces (cBCIs) for precise cognitive rehabilitation and performance optimization of rTMS intervention in depression.

articleTitle: Brain Computer Interfaces for Enhancing Motor Imagery Classification Using EEG Signal
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The aim of signal processing with transformation techniques, is to precisely identify frequencies and extract minute signal variations. Previous studies have employed various time-frequency distributions (TFD) to extract features from electroen-cephalogram (EEG) signals, and nevertheless, there is still space for improvement. This article introduces a sophisticated method for the classification of motor imagery (MI) EEG signals. The objective of this investigation is to generate TFD plots by utilizing pre-proceed data with continuous wavelet transform (CWT). These plots are designed to assist in the identification of the features of each MI EEG class. Subsequently, these plots are applied to the classification of ResNet-20, ResNet-SO, and Long Short- Term Memory (LSTM) models. The LSTM outperforms the ResN et models, as evidenced by experiments. Our results indicate that this method enhances the efficacy of the brain-computer interface (BCI) for MI tasks and provides substantial advantages for biomedical applications.

articleTitle: UNiFY-ESSL: UNIfied Framework for Yielding EEG-Based Emotion Recognition Model with Self-Supervised Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) based emotion recognition shows promise in human-computer interaction and mental health monitoring, but faces challenges in cross-dataset generalization. This study introduces the Unified Framework for EEG-based Emotion Recognition with Self-Supervised Learning (UNiFY-ESSL), combining self-supervised learning (SSL) and advanced sampling techniques to integrate multiple EEG datasets. UNiFY-ESSL utilizes a unified 14-channel setup across all datasets (SEED, DEAP, and DREAMER), allowing consistent preprocessing and feature extraction. This approach adapts datasets with varying initial channel counts (62 for SEED, 32 for DEAP, and 14 for DREAMER) to a common configuration based on DREAMER's channels. The framework explores contrastive learning methods, specifically Simple Contrastive Learning (Sim-CLR) and Contrastive Predictive Coding (CPC), enhanced by a novel stratified sampling scheme. Experiments yield impressive results: SimCLR achieves F1-scores of 82.62%, 87.83%, and 89.05% for SEED, DEAP, and DREAMER respectively, while CPC attains 81.35%, 82.27%, and 91.23%. It demonstrates improved cross-dataset generalization, with a 1–2% performance gain on DREAMER and maintained performance on DEAP despite channel reduction. However, SEED experiences a 3% F1-score drop due to significant channel reduction. These findings highlight the potential of our sampling method in advancing EEG-based emotion recognition while underscoring the need for future work on efficient channel combination strategies, particularly for datasets with higher initial channel counts.

articleTitle: Enhanced U-Net with Transformer-Driven Encoder for Medical Image Segmentation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The automatic segmentation of tumours or lesions from magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) pictures is a critical but difficult task in clinical settings, sometimes necessitating laborious and time-consuming techniques. Deep learning has made a significant advancement in the medical imaging field in recent years. U-Net has emerged as the predominant model used for segmenting medical images. Although the standard U-Net framework has shown excellent performance in segmenting multimodal medical pictures, it has been noticed that it lags in certain aspects when dealing with tough datasets. We propose specific improvements to the state-of-the-art U-Net model. We have introduced attention block in the skipped connections to highlight relevant features. Additionally, we have incorporated transformers in the encoding path to capture temporal dependencies in medical images. In this research work, we have introduced an innovative architecture that has the potential to replace the U-Net model for segmenting regions of interest (ROI) in medical images. This study utilizes a total of 1760 samples obtained from the ISBI 2015 and PH<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> medical repositories. The experimental findings have demonstrated that our proposed model has obtained highly encouraging results of 78.02 Jaccard coefficient and IoU of 65.14. In addition, we conducted tests and compared the performance of the proposed model with the classical U-Net model using the same dataset. As a result, we observed a relative improvement in the performance of both 2.36 and 1.85, respectively. The proposed technology will function as a sophisticated toolkit for radiologists to precisely detect and diagnose anomalous tumour cells.

articleTitle: Deciphering Braille: EEG Based Deep Learning for Character Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The study of experience-based plasticity in the human cortex, especially in those who lost eyesight at birth or early in life, provides valuable insights into the brain's ability to adjust to sensory loss. This study examines how the brain reorganises to map tactile information, such as Braille, by shifting functions from vision to touch processing areas. The work employs EEG to track the transition from sensory to perceptual representations, revealing spatiotemporal changes. These findings have major implications for Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) technologies. Understanding how the brain repurposes regions for different sensory modalities might help researchers develop BCI designs to compensate sensory deficiencies, improve neural signal interpretation, and guide user behaviour effectively. Integrating neural adaptation insights with BCI development can enhance assistive technology to better meet the needs of individuals with sensory disorders. This study explores how the brain responds to braille letter recognition, a crucial aspect of tactile reading for persons with visual impairments. We ued statistical and deep learning based techniques to categorise braille representations in the brain. LSTM achieved 88.9% accuracy in categorising left-vs-right hands, while CNN scored 20.3% accuracy across eight classes. Deep learning outperformed machine learning method across both the scenarios.

articleTitle: EEG Signal Analysis to Verify the Impact of Music on Human Emotions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Emotions are a vital aspect of humanity and under-standing them is one of the most challenging tasks. In our study, EEG data was collected from 10 healthy subjects, comprising 5 males and 5 females by using a 3-electrode system. The experiment involved assessing EEG signals across four stages with various stimuli to evoke emotions, particularly focusing on changes while subjects listened to music. We used both statistical analysis and machine learning algorithm to classify emotions based on time-domain features extracted from EEG signal data. Statistical analysis revealed emotional variations during music listening, indicated by changes in the Root Mean Square (RMS) value. By using machine learning, we classified six discrete emotions (Happy, Enjoy, Calm, Sad, Excited, Bored) and arousal and valence states using five classifiers: Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN), Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP), Random Forest, and Decision Tree. This approach effectively distinguished each emotional states and provided insights into arousal and valence states.

articleTitle: One-Class SVM Using Domain-Based sEMG Features for Detection of Neuromuscular Disorders
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Neuromuscular Disorders (NMDs) are a group of conditions that affect nerves and muscles leading to muscle weakness, atrophy, and sometimes paralysis. The effects of these conditions cannot be reversed, causing permanent impairment if not diagnosed timely. Recent medical advancements have led to timely detection and successful prevention of many diseases with portable healthcare solutions backed by strong machine learning algorithms. A similar approach for NMDs can be designed using non-invasive Surface Electromyography (sEMG) signals. While machine learning approaches have been developed for detecting NMDs, generalized features and a lack of comprehensive datasets prevent the evaluation of the robustness of these methods. Thus, a systematic methodology that incorporates features representing NMD biomarkers and one-class support vector machine for unsupervised detection of neuromuscular disorders is proposed. The method is implemented on electromyography analysis of Human Activity – Database 1 (EMAHA DB-1) which is a comprehensive dataset for hand gesture recognition based on Indian population. For robust evaluation of the algorithm, functions are designed to simulate anomalies based on NMD bio-signals' knowledge by generating an augmented dataset that mimics the nature of NMDs. Multiple machine learning models are implemented and evaluated on the real healthy dataset as well as simulated NMDs dataset. One-class SVM emerged successful amongst other models with an accuracy of 81.45%, averaged over separately trained models for each limb action.

articleTitle: Data-Driven Approach for Medical Competency Assessment Using VR Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The medical education in India urgently needs advanced training tools like virtual reality (VR) to improve Objective Structured Clinical Exams (OSCEs) and National Exit Test (NExT) assessments. The SimX Virtual Manikin Series offers a customizable solution, enhancing medical simulation education through realistic, interactive patient scenarios. These virtual patients allow real-time adjustments to avatars, environments, and clinical situations, addressing the limitations of traditional manikins that cannot simulate complex symptoms or interactions. Instructors can modify patient appearance, vitals, animations, and even dialogue, enabling learners to practice and demonstrate critical skills such as communication, clinical reasoning, and physical examination in a controlled environment. The system's adaptability ensures a more engaging and dynamic learning experience. Learners can repeatedly practice various scenarios, ensuring consistent training. Competency is assessed based on scores for each skill, aligned with India's competency-based medical education standards. The study suggests that this innovative VR approach can significantly enhance the preparation of medical students for real-world challenges, offering a fair and comprehensive assessment method. This research highlights VR's potential to revolutionize medical education in India, providing faster, more effective training and setting a new benchmark for competency assessment in healthcare.

articleTitle: Emotion Detection Mastery: EEG Signal Analysis with Balanced vs. Unbalanced Data
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Emotion is crucial in daily life, influencing stress levels, decision-making, relationships, and overall mental health. Recognizing emotions accurately is valuable across sectors like healthcare, education, and beyond. This paper presents a comparative study on emotion recognition, applying various deep learning models with the DEAP dataset, which includes EEG recordings from 32 participants who watched 40 short music video clips. We extracted time-domain, frequency-domain, and wavelet features from the preprocessed EEG data to capture nuanced patterns within the signals. The models assessed in this study include convolutional neural networks (CNN), long short-term memory networks (LSTM), gated recurrent units (GRU), and hybrid architectures, each trained on both balanced and unbalanced datasets. To address class imbalance, data was augmented using the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE). Results indicate that the Attention GRU model achieved slightly higher performance by utilizing its attention mechanism to capture extended dependencies within the data. Additionally, model accuracy improved by 5-9% when trained on balanced datasets, underscoring the importance of data balancing in enhancing classification outcomes.

articleTitle: Enhancement of Fetal Brain Ultrasound Image via Anatomical ROI Extraction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The precision of fetal biometric measurements in obstetric examinations highly relies on the quality of the acquired Ultrasound Images(US). Biometric measurements of the head such as the head circumference has a direct correlation with gestational age, which if measured incorrectly can lead to poor labour outcomes. Progressive enhancement of the acquired fetal head US images reduces the noise and improves the image quality. This leads to better diagnosis, paving the way for accurate measurements thereby facilitating precise fetal growth estimation. This paper demonstrates a two-step process where the ROI is first extracted prior to image enhancement. The ROI extraction has been simplified using a novel two-coordinate method to extract the clinically relevant anatomical region. The image is enhanced by targeted noise reduction, feature enhancement and artifact removal, highlighting the critical anatomical structures and ensuring clear visualization of the fetal brain US image. The effectiveness of the proposed method is evaluated using image quality assessing metrics such as Naturalness Image Quality Evaluator (NIQE), Blind/Referenceless Image Quality Evaluator(BRISQUE) and Perception-Based Image Quality Evaluator(PIQE) with an increase in score by 13%, 29.34%, and 20.5% respectively, demonstrating significant improvements in image clarity and detail retention. This enhancement process could equip obstetricians to perform precise fetal head biometry measurements and thus has substantial applicability in advanced ultrasound imaging scenarios.

articleTitle: IoT-Based Fall Detection and Airbag Deployment System for Enhanced Elderly Care Using NodeMCU ESP8266 and MPU6050 Sensor
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: The aging population faces significant risks from falls, often leading to fractures, head injuries, and extended hospitalization. To mitigate these dangers, an integrated solution combining fall detection and an airbag protection system is proposed using NodeMCU ESP8266 and the MPU6050 sensor. The system accurately detects falls, generates alerts, provides notification messages, and tracks the location in real time. Upon fall detection, it also triggers an airbag that inflates via an inflation pump to minimize the impact on critical body parts. The proposed model achieved 93 % accuracy and 95 % sensitivity, demonstrating its reliability in enhancing safety and improving the overall well-being and quality of life for the elderly.

articleTitle: Revolutionizing Endoscopic Diagnostics: A Comparative Study of DC-UNet and MC-UNet
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Endoscopic imaging plays a pivotal role in diag-nosing and managing gastrointestinal diseases, where precise segmentation of images is essential for accurate disease detection and treatment. Traditional image segmentation methods often struggle with the complexities inherent in endoscopic images, prompting the development of advanced deep-learning models. This paper compares two novel architectures designed to improve segmentation performance: the dual-channel U-Net (DC-UNet) and the multi-channel U-Net (MC-UNet). The DC-UNet model builds on the traditional U-Net framework by incorporating dilated convolutions and residual modules to enhance feature extraction and improve segmentation accuracy. Dilated convo-lutions increase the receptive field without sacrificing spatial resolution, while residual modules facilitate better information flow across the network's layers. In addition, we present the MC-UNet, which extends the DC-UNet architecture by integrating multi-channels to capture features at varying resolutions and improve the detection of structures of different sizes. We evaluate the performance of both models on two challenging endoscopy image datasets: Kvasir-Instrument and CVC-ClinicDB. The DC-UNet achieved an accuracy of 97.34% on Kvasir-Instrument and 97.98% on CVC-ClinicDB, while the MC-UNet demonstrated slighter better performance with 98.25% and 98.19% accuracy, respectively. Our results highlight the potential of the DC-UNet and MC-UNet models to revolutionise endoscopic diagnostics by providing more accurate and reliable segmentation results, ultimately improving clinical outcomes.

articleTitle: Image Restoration and Enhancement of Retinal images Using Multi-Resolution Dual CNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: In this paper we propose a Multi-resolution Dual Convolutional Neural Network (MR-DCNN) which is used to denoise the images. By incorporating sparse mechanism in dual networks, implementing a 2-tier architecture and by downscaling the width and height of CNN layers, we could reduce the computational complexity and achieve better performance and speed. The observed values prove that the novel MR-DCNN method can upgrade the visual quality without even compromising on PSNR, SSIM and MSE values. The suggested MR DCNN method outperforms numerous modern image enhancing techniques, based on objective and subjective results. Later, we propose the MR-DCNN method to boost the visual quality of low contrast retinal images. The MR-DCNN incorporated helps to enhance the visual quality by denoising the images and also removing fading effects. This novel formulation attains further improvement than existing schemes, and proves significant development in PSNR, SSIM and MSE values and visual quality perception. The presented scheme enhances the retinal image quality by improving the clarity. The MR-DCNN approach could deliver ophthalmologists with novel strategies to rectify retinal diseases from fundus images. This will lessen the amount of manual grading required, which will assist to cut down on pointless, expensive referrals.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of CNN Architectures With Transfer Learning for Brain Tumor Detection and Classification From MRI Scans
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: In the realm of neuroscience, one of the most profound topics of investigation is brain tumors, as they greatly influence brain operations and overall health. These brain tumors can be classified into two types. The two types are malignant and benign tumors. While deadly by mere spreading towards different organs of the human body, illed abnormal masses of cells such as gliomas are notorious in making great harm to people's central nervous system. Conversely, though benign types do not pose imminent danger to life, their presence could still result in significant neurological disturbances. The three primary varieties of brain related tumors are classified as glial cell-based gliomas, meninges based meningiomas and finally pituitary gland based pituitary tumors. During the recent past, we have witnessed deep learning (DL) being a successful methodology in the spotting and categorizing of various types of brain tumors. The Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) is the most popular method in the DL to be used in such scenarios. The study at hand evaluates several existing CNN architectures such as VGG16, Inception, Xception and DenseNet121 with respect to their performance in classifying brain tumors. This research aims at finding out which one among these is the most suited architecture in terms of precision and efficiency in diagnosing human brain tumors so that it can help improve automatic devices used in neurology and other medical fields.

articleTitle: Bacterial Contamination Monitoringand Prevention in Chambers Using Post Processing Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: An innovative approach to monitoring and preventing bacterial contamination within chamber sthrough a combination of pressure control and post-processingtechniques is presented. The proposed system integrates real-time monitoring mechanisms with semi-automatic prevention measures to mitigate the risk of bacterial dispersion. Central to this system is the utilization of pressure control mechanisms to prevent the escape of bacteria into the surrounding air, ensuring containment within the chamber. Additionally, post-processing methods employing heat and UVC sterilization are implemented to eliminate any residual bacteria present within the chamber environment. Experimental results demonstrate that bacteria such as Salmonella typhi and Mycobacteriumtuberculosis are effectively eradicated, with the system achieving over 99.9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> sterilization efficiency. The synergy between monitoring, pressure control, and post-processing ensures comprehensive protection against bacterial contamination, enhancing safety and efficacy in various applications such as medical, research, and industrial settings. This paper discusses the theoretical framework, implementation details, and potential applications of the proposed system, highlighting its effectiveness in maintaining sterile environments and safeguarding against bacterials pread.

articleTitle: Identification of Affective States from Malayalam Audios Based on Valence Arousal Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Affective state plays a key role in emotion recognition, influencing various applications from mental health evaluation to human-machine interaction. These states can be described using two primary aspects: valence, which indicates the pleasantness of the speech, and arousal, which relates to the intensity of the emotion. This study aims to automate the prediction of valence and arousal values from speech data, addressing the limitations of manual annotation and human error. The IIITSAINT-EMOMDB dataset, created from Malayalam films, uses the Circumplex Model of Affect to map emotions such as happy, sad, angry, and calm. The approach leverages machine learning models, including Support Vector Regression (SVR), Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), for prediction. Experimental results demonstrate that the traditional models like SVR and ANN are outperformed by the CNN model, which achieved a mean squared error (MSE) of 0.3 for valence and 0.1 for arousal. These findings highlight the power of automated emotion recognition in large-scale audio datasets, offering promising applications in affective computing and psychological analysis.

articleTitle: Enhancing Autism Detection in MRI Images with Explainable AI: A Transfer Learning Approach Using GradCAM
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a complex neurodevelopmental condition that requires early and accurate diagnosis to facilitate effective treatment. This study aims to enhance diagnostic accuracy for ASD using MRI images while improving interpretability in medical image classification through advanced machine learning techniques. We propose a modified R esNet50 architecture integrated with dual attention mechanisms-Self-Attention and Convolutional Block Attention Module (CBAM)—and utilize Grad-CAM for visual explanations of model predictions. This approach leverages transfer learning from pre-trained CNN models. Using the ABIDE dataset, the dual attention-enhanced ResNet50 achieved a classification accuracy of 97%, outperforming other models in precision, recall, and F1 score. The GradCAM analysis reveals significant activation in subcortical and cortical midline structures. Key subcortical regions, particularly the thalamus, corpus callosum, and cingulate gyrus, which are crucial structures in ASD research. Although these neuroimaging findings provide valuable insights into the neural basis of autism, they should be considered as supportive evidence within a comprehensive clinical diagnostic framework rather than as standalone diagnostic markers. These findings underscore the model's potential as a valuable diagnostic tool for ASD, emphasizing both high accuracy and interpretability. Future research will focus on validating the model across Indian populations and incorporating other explainability techniques to enhance its robustness and applicability.

articleTitle: Cognitive Ergonomic Evaluation of Mental Fatigue for Different Exam Patterns Using EEG
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Two prevalent exam formats, multiple-choice questions (MCQ) and descriptive exams, are common in evaluating students' academic performance. Analyzing the mental fatigue experienced with these formats is essential for their mental well-being. This study aims to investigate mental fatigue (MF) using electroencephalogram (EEG) to obj ectively measure and compare the magnitude of higher frequency brain waves that are enhanced during cognitive performance between the two exam formats of male and female students to assess mental fatigue levels. The methodology includes conducting MCQs and descriptive patterns of exams for 10 females and 10 males of age group 20±2 years and EEG was recorded. The Fast Fourier Transform was performed to evaluate mental fatigue based on different frequency bands of EEG. The spectrum analysis is made for the 0.5 to 30 Hz frequency range, which signifies the delta, theta, alpha, and beta waveforms. The Wilcoxon signed rank test (paired samples) was assigned for comparing MF of MCQ vs. MF of descriptive in females and MF of MCQ vs. MF of descriptive in males. The result shows that the female students experience higher mental fatigue during MCQ exams compared to descriptive exams (p< 0.05), but no evident significant difference in male students. Additionally, an online survey was conducted among 100 students of the same age group, which has confirmed the results obtained in the EEG-based objective assessment. Hence a gender-based mental fatigue comparison was made between female and male students during MCQ and descriptive exam patterns.

articleTitle: Classification of Diabetic Retinopathy Disease Using GNN
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) is a prominent global cause of blindness, requiring labor-intensive manual examinations of fundus images for diagnosis. While convolutional neural networks (CNNs) have shown promise in automating DR diagnosis, they often struggle to retain essential information. This study is driven by the urgent need to prevent DR-related blindness and the importance of early intervention in halting disease progression. Additionally, the aim to mitigate visual impairments and complications associated with DR. To accomplish these objectives, the aim is developing an automated diagnostic system that utilizes Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) to accurately detect and grade DR based on fundus images. The goals include advancing lesion representation, achieving multi-lesion detection and classification, and ensuring robust performance across diverse datasets. By pioneering the use of GNNs in this context, the system promises to revolutionize early DR detection and management by redefining DR classification as a multi-label detection and classification task, ultimately enhancing diagnostic precision. The model generates an accuracy of 87.8% along with lesions being represented in a correlation dependency matrix. This project represents a significant step in the field of DR diagnosis and severity grading, with the potential to significantly improve patient outcomes, reduce the risk of vision loss in diabetic individuals, and contribute to the broader medical community's efforts to combat DR and elevate patient care.

articleTitle: Simpler BCI by Neurological Analysis of Eyeblink and Jaw Clench Events
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: This paper introduces a prototype Brain-Computer Interface (BCI) system designed to facilitate assistive communication for individuals with disabilities using an EEG headset. The system features an intuitive interface enabling users to initiate calls through eyeblinks and jaw clenches. A graphical display presents four selectable contact images, allowing users to navigate and activate calls by blinking and clenching their jaw. The design emphasizes enhancing accessibility and usability in real-time communication scenarios. The scope of this initiative encompasses the development of a BCI system tailored specifically for disabled users, addressing critical performance criteria. The resulting interface is envisioned in two configurations: a standalone system and a mobile interface. These innovations aim to advance accessibility and usability standards, offering practical solutions for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Machine Learning-Enhanced Solutions for Mitigating PCOS/PCOD-Related Women's Health Disparities in Rural Areas: A Holistic Telemedicine System Design and Implementation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Telemedicine plays a crucial role in modern healthcare by providing remote medical services that enhance access and equity, particularly in underserved areas. Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCDS) and polycystic ovarian disorder (PCOD) are prevalent reproductive health issues that significantly impact women globally. Access to gynecological care in remote regions is often hindered by a shortage of specialists, transportation challenges, cultural barriers, and low health literacy, resulting in delayed diagnoses and untreated conditions that can increase maternal and neonatal mortality rates. This paper presents a telemedicine initiative aimed at empowering women by offering essential gynecological services for PCDS and PCOD, regardless of geographical constraints. The platform includes remote video consultations, menstrual cycle tracking, educational resources, and appointment reminders, facilitated by Accredited Social Health Activist (ASHA) workers. These findings illustrate the effectiveness of this approach in improving healthcare access for women, promoting a more equitable future. Additionally, we introduce a machine learning model utilizing a Random Forest algorithm for patient classification based on PCDS and PCOD symptoms. Trained on an 80/20 split dataset, the model's accuracy is evaluated using confusion matrices. This study represents a significant step toward bridging geographical disparities in rural India and providing quality gynecological care.

articleTitle: Dynamic Emotion Regulation through Reinforcement Learning: A Neurofeedback System with EEG Data and Custom Wearable Interventions
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Neurofeedback, a form of biofeedback that uses brainwave activity to provide real-time feedback, is a powerful approach for emotion regulation. Recent advancements in affective computing and machine learning offer new possibilities for improving the efficacy of neurofeedback systems, particularly through adaptive algorithms for personalizing the intervention process. This study presents an innovative neurofeedback mecha-nism that uses reinforcement learning (RL) to regulate emotions. The system uses Q-learning algorithm to dynamically adjusts its intervention strategies based on sampled EEG data from the DEAP dataset that monitors brain activity associated with emotional states. The therapeutic interventions consist of a mix of music therapy sessions, mindfulness exercises, and tactile feedback provided by a custom-built wearable device. The device utilizes tactile vibration as a neurofeedback signal to help users become more conscious of and effectively regulate their emotional well-being. The system's performance was evaluated through detailed analysis of the Q-learning process and observing how various states, actions and rewards influenced effective emotional regulation. Using sampled EEG data from the DEAP dataset enabled comprehensive testing and refinement of the system's algorithms in a controlled environment, thereby setting the stage for potential future use with real time EEG devices. The results of this study highlight the power of RL-based neurofeedback to help transform emotional wellbeing, while also showcasing the potential to expand the spectrum of neurofeedback tools to be more responsive and adaptive to individual users, ultimately promoting improved mental health.

articleTitle: EEG Based Deep Learning Model for Automated Classification of Frequent and Infrequent Readers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Reading comprehension is a complex cognitive process that involves semantic decoding, and schema integration influenced by reading practice. This study investigates the neural correlates of reading comprehension and explores how brain activation patterns differ between frequent and infrequent readers. Using Electroencephalography (EEG), the brain activation patterns were recorded from participants while performing the reading comprehension tasks. The EEG signal is recorded with a sampling rate of 1024 Hz to capture the dynamic changes in brain activation during reading tasks, revealing how frequent and infrequent readers differ in their cognitive processing and neural efficiency. The 21 channels of EEG signal acquired from 9 participants were pre-processed to obtain a 512 Hz band-limited signal. The pre-processed EEG signals were segmented before being fed into a twenty-four-layered convolutional neural network (CNN) model. The convolution stage extracts the temporal and spatial features, and the most significant features are extracted at the max-pooling stage. Frequent and infrequent readers are classified using the fully connected layer based on their EEG signals. The proposed model obtained a classification accuracy of 93.94%.

articleTitle: Optimization of Artificial Neural Network Modelling for Improving Diabetic Diagnosis: A Promising Approach for Early Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Diabetes impacts food-to-energy conversion and is chronic. Diabetics store glucose in their blood instead of using it for energy, causing major health issues. The WHO reports that diabetes is rising worldwide, and early detection and treatment are crucial to preventing complications. Artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) techniques have the potential to revolutionize the diagnosis of diabetes by making it possible to identify people at risk earlier and diagnose it more accurately. This work introduces a supervised learning approach in the artificial neural network (ANN) to improve the accuracy of diabetes diagnosis. Eight input variables from the National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases dataset were used, including 2000 patients with 65.8% healthy and 34.2% diabetic. Altering the feedforward backpropagation neural network architecture improved the ANN's accuracy. Changes were made to hidden layers (1 to 3) and neurons (20 to 100) using R2 and MSE. The ANN model suited the dataset well with R2 and MSE of 99.1% and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$7.38\times 10-6$</tex> in the optimal architecture. These results imply that the suggested method might quickly detect diabetes.

articleTitle: Epilepsy Detection: Neural Network With PSO-Based Feature Selection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Epilepsy is a persistent neurological condition marked by recurring, spontaneous seizures caused by unusual electrical brain activity. The nature and intensity of these seizures can vary greatly, spanning from momentary distractions or muscle twitches to severe and extended convulsions. Early detection and diagnosis are crucial to manage epilepsy effectively, as timely intervention with medications and other therapeutic strategies can help control seizures and improve quality of life for those affected. Electroencephalogram (EEG) is widely used diagnostic tool for recognizing abnormal activities of brain and helps to identify epilepsy cases but it is very time consuming,prone to artifacts and vary with the interpreter's experience. This study aims to develop a robust and efficient algorithm to detect different stages of epilepsy from EEG data. The proposed approach integrates Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) for feature selection with a deep learning neural network to improve the accuracy and reliability of seizure detection. The detection model uses the features extracted from complete ensemble empirical based decomposed EEG signals. Features are optimized by Particle Swarm Organization which is input into classifier employing the artificial neural network (ANN)mechanism. Employing these methods, pre-ictal, ictal and inter-ictal stages of epilepsy is identified in EEG. The proposed approach successfully classified these epileptic stages with an accuracy of 98.33%. This enhanced epilepsy detection system holds significant potential for improving patient outcomes through early and accurate detection of seizures, providing a robust tool for neurologists and healthcare providers in the management of epilepsy.

articleTitle: Tapping the Differences Between Reward Processes and Executive Control for Efficient Brain-Machine Interfacing (BMI) Recovery in Post-Stroke Patients with Upper Limb Impairments
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on Brain Computer Interface & Healthcare Technologies (iCon-BCIHT)
abstract: Stroke is one of the leading causes of disability and death worldwide. Advanced technologies such as Brain Machine/Computer Interfaces (BMI/BCI) can improve the efficacy of rehabilitation therapies through a multidisciplinary approach using robotic exoskeletons for motor recovery. In such interfaces, exploring the network-level understanding of the source space, in terms of various cognitive dimensions such as executive control versus reward processing, is fruitful in both improving the existing therapy protocols and understanding the subject-level differences. We analyzed data from two stroke patients from a published study involving a BMI-based intervention for upper limb recovery, with simultaneously recorded electroencephalography (EEG) and electromyography (EMG) signals. In that study, patients had to make both a movement ‘intention’ detected by an EEG classifier and an ‘attempt’ captured by EMG signals to successfully drive the exoskeleton to reach a cue displayed on the screen. We have performed source localization on their EEG data and found three significant observations. Successful trials (both movement intention and attempt were present) revealed relatively strong effective connectivity between frontoparietal and cingulo-opercular networks (FPN-CON), and between the right Anterior Cingulate and Anterior Cingulate Cortex (ACC), each associated with executive function and attention, respectively. Furthermore, we observed reduced entorhinal beta power for successful trials implying reward maximization and higher attention. Altogether, our study proposes a novel cognitively adaptable BMI design that taps at the functional connectivity representatives of cognitive functions such as attention, reward processing, and execution, for efficient design and precise, personalized performance recovery.
